title: Bushels Kept Pledged Against a Marketing Commitment
content:
Bushels the member has already committed onto a marketing contract are not free either, and they are carried in the same pledged figure, the bushels applied being counted as the net bushels the delivery entry credits to the contract rather than the gross weigh across the scale. This rule governs Grain Storage and Conditioning Agreements and reads the member's position under Grain Marketing Contracts.

## What the schedule provides

Where fifteen thousand bushels or more stand open on active marketing contracts for the same commodity and no bushels have been applied to them in the last three months, the whole of the bushels still open stays pledged.

Where bushels stand open on an active marketing contract for the same commodity, or bushels have been applied to the member's marketing contracts in the last three months, the bushels still open less the bushels applied over those three months stays pledged, and never less than nothing.

And otherwise nothing stays pledged for a marketing commitment.

## The two records read

The first is the bushels still open on the member's active contracts under Grain Marketing Contracts for the same commodity as the stored lot. The second is the bushels applied to the member's contracts over the last three months, taken from the delivery entries in that product's ledger that were applied to a contract; the quantity counted on each such entry is the net bushels it credits to the contract, not the gross weigh across the scale.

| Bushels open on active contracts for the same commodity | Bushels applied over the last three months | Kept pledged |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 15000 or more | none at all | the whole of the bushels still open |
| 15000 or more | some | the bushels still open less the bushels applied, never below nothing |
| more than nil but under 15000 | any quantity | the bushels still open less the bushels applied, never below nothing |
| none | more than nil | the bushels still open less the bushels applied, never below nothing |
| none | none | nothing |

The threshold is read as at or above: exactly 15000 bushels open with nothing applied takes the first line.

## Worked holdbacks, on hypothetical figures

**Eighteen thousand bushels open on active corn contracts, nothing applied over the three months.** The whole 18000 stays pledged.

**Eighteen thousand bushels open, 5000 applied over the three months.** Eighteen thousand less five thousand leaves 13000 pledged.

**Four thousand bushels open, 6000 applied over the three months.** Four thousand less six thousand falls below nothing, so nothing stays pledged for the commitment.

**Nothing open and nothing applied.** Nothing stays pledged for a marketing commitment.
